title: Channel interface, operator config, and fake channel (contract)
description:
New package internal/operator. Defines the contract every channel implements and the config it persists — everything later ticks build against.

- Channel interface sized to ask/tell: Send(text) error; AskDeliver(Question) (MessageRef, error); Events(ctx) <-chan Event (answer text, option press, multi-select commit); Resolve(MessageRef, Outcome) error (post-resolution message edit / button removal).
- Question/Event/Outcome types mirror AskUserQuestion semantics: question text, options with label+description, multi-select flag, allow-other flag.
- Global config: LoadOperatorConfig/SaveOperatorConfig for ~/.ticks/operator.json — per-channel map, e.g. {"telegram":{"token","user_id","chat_id","bot_username","api_base"}}. Honor TICKS_HOME env override (tests). Write 0600, parent dir 0700.
- FakeChannel (in-memory) implementing the interface with scriptable events — the test double every ask/tell test in epic 2 will use.

Test cases:
- Save then Load round-trips config; file mode is 0600.
- TICKS_HOME redirects the path; missing file → zero-value config, no error.
- FakeChannel: AskDeliver + scripted event arrives on Events; Resolve records outcome.
Run: go test -short -count=1 ./internal/operator/...
